title: Cannabis Plant Anatomy and Developmental Organization
summary: Cannabis cultivation decisions make more sense when leaves, nodes, meristems, roots and reproductive structures are understood as an integrated developmental system rather than isolated plant parts.

sections.title: Meristems organize new growth
sections.body: Shoot and root meristems contain actively dividing tissues that generate new organs and determine where future leaves, branches, roots and reproductive structures can arise. Training and propagation practices work by interacting with this developmental organization, not by creating growth independently of plant biology.

sections.title: Nodes connect architecture and reproduction
sections.body: Nodes are repeating structural units where leaves, axillary shoots and reproductive structures can develop. Node number, spacing and branch behavior therefore provide useful morphological context for vegetative stage, canopy structure and later reproductive scouting.

sections.title: Roots and shoots are physiologically coupled
sections.body: Roots acquire water and mineral nutrients while shoots create much of the transpiration demand and photosynthetic carbon that supports root growth. Changes in light, humidity, irrigation or root-zone oxygen can therefore produce whole-plant responses rather than remaining confined to one organ.
